before.jp: 力が出ません。
before.kana: ちからがでません。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence follows the basic Japanese order: topic/subject + particle + verb at the end. 力 (strength) is marked by が as the thing that 'doesn't come out', and the verb 出る (to come out, to arise) is in the polite negative form 出ません. The grammar target 〜ません is the polite negative: take the verb's masu-stem (出ます) and change ます to ません to negate politely. Literally 'strength doesn't come out', but in English it sounds natural as 'I have no strength / I'm out of energy'.

O alvo gramatical 〜ません é o negativo polido: pega-se a raiz do verbo na forma-ます (出ます) e troca-se ます por ません para negar com cortesia. Literalmente 'a força não sai', mas em pt-BR soa natural como 'não tenho forças / estou sem energia'.

before.jp: 来月はとても忙しいだろう。

structure_explanation.en: The i-adjective 忙しい (busy) is followed directly by だろう, the grammar focus (i-adjectives don't need だ before だろう). Here だろう expresses supposition/prediction about the future ('I'll probably be busy'). とても (very) intensifies the adjective, and は marks 来月 (next month) as the temporal topic.

Aqui だろう expressa suposição/previsão sobre o futuro ('provavelmente estarei ocupado'). とても (muito) intensifica o adjetivo, e は marca 来月 (mês que vem) como tópico temporal.

before.jp: 来月このアパートから引っ越すんです。

structure_explanation.en: 来月 ('next month') opens as a time reference. このアパートから uses the demonstrative この ('this') + から marking the point of origin of the movement ('from this apartment'). The verb 引っ越す ('to move house') is in the dictionary form. The closing んです (ん = contracted の + です) gives the explanatory tone: the person not only informs, but contextualizes/justifies the move.

before.jp: 来月１７歳になるのですか。

structure_explanation.en: A question of whether the person will turn 17 next month. 来月 ('next month') is the time adjunct. １７歳 ('17 years of age', the number 17 + the suffix 歳) links to に + なる, which is the target 〜になる ('to become'): literally 'to become 17 years of age', that is, 'to turn 17'. のですか gives the tone of an explanatory/confirmatory question.

ops.issue: 来る日 = 'the coming day' (attributive 来る), not 'the day before' — the literal gloss inverts the time direction and contradicts expl_en and lit_pt ('dia que vem').

before.jp: 来る日も来る日も雨だった。
before.kana: くるひもくるひもあめだった。

structure_explanation.en: The expression 来る日も来る日も ('day after day', literally 'both the coming day and the coming day') is a fixed formula of repetition, reinforced by も…も ('both… and / even'). The grammatical focus is at the end: 雨だった = 'it was rain / it rained', in which だった is the simple past of the copula だ. It is the structure [noun + だった] = 'was/were'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A expressão 来る日も来る日も ('dia após dia', literalmente 'tanto no dia que vem quanto no dia que vem') é uma fórmula fixa de repetição, reforçada por も…も ('tanto… quanto / até'). O foco gramatical está no fim: 雨だった = 'era chuva / chovia', em que だった é o passado simples da cópula だ. É a estrutura [substantivo + だった] = 'foi/era'.

translation_literal.en: The day before (too) and the day before that (too), it was rain (datta).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Dia que vem (também) dia que vem (também) chuva, era (だった).

translation.pt-BR: Chovia dia após dia.
